newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end up but off record high.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end up but off record high.

text.p: Jakarta share prices broke new ground on Wednesday but profit-taking pulled them back from a record high for the composite index of 687.65, brokers said.
The index closed up 5.24 points, or 0.77 percent, on the day at 686.12 points after peaking at 687.65. The previous record of 681.94 points was achieved on April 4, 1990.
Gainers led losers by 95 to 40, with 51 counters unchanged. Total volume was 400.2 million shares on a turnover of 754.57 billion rupiah.
"Technically, the market still has the potential to maintain the upside level tomorrow," a foreign broker said.

He said that even if the market experienced some correction, the index would continue to gain as foreign and local buying interest in selected stocks, such as heavyweight Bank Negara Indonesia, was still high.
But a Singaporean analyst said the index might stay within a narrow range on Thursday as the market was likely to undergo a consolidation period after the sharp rises of the last week.
Bank Negara Indonesia traded heavily as the most active stock, up 25 rupiah to 1,575 on 86.8 million shares on expectations of higher 1996 earnings, brokers said.

They said the bank, with an index weight of 2.6 percent, and increases in other heavyweights like telecommunications firm Telkom and toll road operator Citra Marga, had helped boost overall market sentiment.
Telkom rose 100 rupiah to 4,250 rupiah on 7.3 million shares, while Citra Marga rose 125 rupiah to 2,150 rupiah on 8.9 million shares on fresh buying on their fundamentals, brokers said.

They said many local investors were reacting to the upward momentum by snapping up certain small and cheap stocks like transportation firm Centris, marble producer Citatah and textile companies Apac Centertex and Ever Shine Tex.
But blue chip cigarette maker Gudang Garam fell 3.14 percent to 12,225 rupiah on a volume of 526,500 shares on profit taking, brokers said.
Analysts and brokers said the fall in Gudang Garam, the second heaviest stock in Jakarta with an index weighting of 10.46 percent, had helped pull the index off its record high.
